comments.author: runlevel1
comments.story: Axon wants to make taser drones for schools despite ethics board’s concerns
comments.why: Dramatization of fully autonomous attack drones and why the threat is serious.
comments.text: Why require RF at all? An attacker could give the drone a location they know their target will be at and let the drone autonomously guide itself to the target. [This dramatization][^1] focuses on full autonomy, but I'd argue it applies just as much to the steps leading up to it. All the more reason to take this threat seriously now. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.text: I think it depends, right? If you have a small number of high cost, high impact UAVs, you will target infra and supply columns. If you happen to have a cargo plane full of cheap, mass produced head-popper slaughterbots which you can dump over a town, they will remove all the humans and leave you with intact buildings, vehicles, and infra. comments.text: I know it is rather sensationalized, but how far off is this kind of technology? [VIDEO] "Slaughterbots" posted in 2017. If I had to guess, I'd say that the tiny drones in this video still aren't capable of carrying the computational horsepower necessary for a lot of the activities portrayed. But...isn't it really a matter of time?
